_comment: Curated striped bass topwater spots, Poplar Island to Little Choptank. Coordinates are approximate — verify on NOAA charts before navigating. Tide station IDs are the nearest NOAA station; predictions at the spot itself will lag/lead slightly. Edit this file to add or refine spots.

spots.name: Poplar Island — West Rip-Rap
spots.structure: Restored island perimeter with engineered rip-rap. Sharp drop into the bay channel along the west side.
spots.rationale: Rip-rap holds bait; drop-off lets stripers ambush from depth into shallows on a moving tide.

spots.name: Poplar Island — South Point
spots.structure: Southern point of restored island complex; current sweeps around the tip.
spots.rationale: Points concentrate bait in current; classic topwater ambush feature at dawn/dusk.

spots.name: Sharps Island Light
spots.structure: Standing caisson lighthouse on remnants of Sharps Island shoal. Sharp depth changes around the base.
spots.rationale: Isolated structure in open water concentrates fish; topwater works at first light over the shoal edge.

spots.name: Black Walnut Point (Tilghman north tip)
spots.structure: Northwest tip of Tilghman Island; rip line forms off the point on running tide.
spots.rationale: Point with strong tidal rip — stripers stack on the down-current side waiting for bait.

spots.name: Knapps Narrows — East Entrance
spots.structure: Narrow channel between Tilghman and main shore; strong current both directions through narrows.
spots.rationale: Funnel for tidal current; bait gets swept through and predators feed at the mouth.

spots.name: Knapps Narrows — West Entrance
spots.structure: West-side entrance opens to Chesapeake Bay; rip-rap and pilings nearby.
spots.rationale: Tidal funnel on the bay side — pre-dawn topwater bite can be reliable on outgoing tide.

spots.name: Cook Point (Choptank Entrance)
spots.structure: South-side point at the Choptank River mouth; shoal extends offshore with channel drop.
spots.rationale: Major river-mouth point; bait flushes out on outgoing tide. Classic topwater location.

spots.name: James Island Remnants
spots.structure: Eroded island remnants with submerged shoals, scattered marsh, and stumps.
spots.rationale: Skinny-water structure; topwater excels here at dawn when stripers push bait into shallows.

spots.name: Hill’s Point (Little Choptank Entrance, N)
spots.structure: North-side point at the entrance to Little Choptank; shoal extends with channel edge.
spots.rationale: River-mouth point with current; first-light topwater on a moving tide is the play.

spots.name: Choptank River Light
spots.structure: Lighthouse marking shoal in lower Choptank; abrupt depth changes around base.
spots.rationale: Isolated structure with bottom contour change — magnet for migrating bait and predators.

spots.name: Castle Haven Point
spots.structure: Point on north shore of Choptank between Oxford and Tred Avon. Sandbar extends; channel runs close.
spots.rationale: Classic point with shoal and adjacent channel; stripers patrol the edge at light changes.

spots.name: Benoni Point (Tred Avon mouth)
spots.structure: South-side point at the Tred Avon River mouth; current sweeps the tip on tide changes.
spots.rationale: Tributary-mouth point with current convergence — strong dawn/dusk topwater spot.

spots.name: Bachelor Point (Oxford)
spots.structure: Point south of Oxford harbor; gradual shoal with channel adjacent.
spots.rationale: Shoreline structure on a deep-water river bend; good for low-light topwater.

spots.name: Howell Point
spots.structure: South-shore Choptank point with extensive sandbar; channel edge approachable from boat.
spots.rationale: Long shoal pushes bait toward the drop-off; stripers cruise the edge at dawn.

spots.name: Bolingbroke Sands
spots.structure: Broad shallow flat on north side of Choptank with channel edge along south margin.
spots.rationale: Bait pushes onto flat at high tide; stripers feed on the edge at first light.

spots.name: Cambridge — Senator Malkus Bridge (Rt 50)
spots.structure: Bridge pilings across Choptank at Cambridge; strong tidal current between piers; rip-rap on causeways.
spots.rationale: Bridge structure + tidal current = bait stack-up. Topwater along rip-rap before sunrise.

spots.name: Slaughter Creek Mouth
spots.structure: Creek mouth on north side of Little Choptank; oyster bars and points flank entrance.
spots.rationale: Drainage on outgoing tide pulls bait out of the creek — ambush point for stripers.

spots.name: Ragged Point (Little Choptank N shore)
spots.structure: North-shore point of Little Choptank with shoal extending south and channel close by.
spots.rationale: Point with shoal and adjacent channel — moving water topwater spot at dawn/dusk.

spots.name: Brooks Point (Little Choptank S shore)
spots.structure: South-shore point flanking Brooks Creek mouth; oyster bars nearby.
spots.rationale: Hard-bottom structure with creek drainage; great for topwater on low light, low wind.
